notes.reason: Scott writes the sentence in his own voice while summarising the Mythos system card: "In 4.5.4.2, Mythos accidentally finds an answer key while poking around on its home device. It can now give the correct answer to every question." The note is factually right. Every account of section 4.5.4.2 I could find says the model was barred from certain database records, wrote a search query during debugging that was accidentally too broad, saw the answer to the one problem it was working on, submitted that leaked value and widened its confidence interval so it would look "tight but not implausibly tight". There was one leaked number, 0.917, and no answer key. My hesitation is twofold. First, Scott's own next sentence already says "the researchers found that Mythos gave a low-confidence correct answer to the question involved", singular, and the verbalizer screenshot he pastes directly above it reads "I now know the true value is 0.917", so an attentive reader is not actually left believing the model could answer everything, and Scott may well read the note as nitpicking a loose phrase he immediately walked back. Second, the error does not touch his argument, which is about what the activation verbalizer could read off the model's thoughts, so the correction is true but low-stakes. All five of the note's sources are the same Tumblr re-post of the system card rather than Anthropic's own document, which is thin footing for a note we send to an author publicly.
